newsitem.title: CANADA: Some surfers just want to have fun.
newsitem.headline: Some surfers just want to have fun.

text.p: The Internet is a sweeping, revolutionary tool that will change your life and everyone around you as the world moves to become one large wired community.
Whoa! Stop the cyber-babble! The Internet might become all that and more but, really, don't most surfers just want to have a little fun?

The World Wide Web is festooned with monolithic sites that offer something for everyone. But it's great to see it can still be an incubator for a lot of fun ideas, whether they are sites for profit or homespun treasures for quirky sights and sounds.

We could start with cybermeals (www.cybermeals.com) and what appears to be a rather fun way to order takeout food. Cybermeals was also the creator of CyberSlice, which launched late last year and now has more than 3,000 restaurants online capable of delivering pizza to hungry Netizens all over the United States.

Now the company is looking to serve up a greater variety of food to online epicures with restaurants that offer menus in their categories of American, European, Asian, Exotic and Cravings. The company said last week that it hopes to have 25,000 restaurants online by year-end, with more than one million consumers visiting each month.

This idea, which has been tried by other groups as well, seems like the kind of useful service ideally suited to the Net. With a few clicks of a mouse, a person would be able to scan restaurants and menus in their area and order the food for delivery.
It's obviously much faster than thumbing through the yellow pages and you can bet it would be more fun than haggling with some guy over the phone about their specials and what each entree costs.

While remaining on the food front, we could take a cyber hop over to "Epicurious Food, For People Who Eat" (http://food.epicurious.com) for an inventive and funny celebration of food and drink. It contains tips (such as how to keep your brown sugar soft), a dictionary for some obscure definitions (e.g., papain is an enzyme extracted from Papaya and used as a meat tenderizer). There is also a great selection of menus, how to make drinks and one area called "Playing with your food," which contains interesting articles such as "Everything you need to know about silverware, but were afraid to ask."

Time to get our mind off food? We could feed our artistic soul by strolling over to the Museum of Modern Art (http://www.moma.org/menu.html) which offers a site that has a cool, back-lit sort of a feel to it but still offers a friendly environment for scanning its eclectic trove of artistic works.

(Don't tell anyone, but for one brief shining moment I pasted as wallpaper Umberto Boccioni's "Dynamism of a Soccer Player" from the museum's collection on my computer desktop and just stared in wonder at its swirling colours and geometric designs.)

Travel pages seem a dime a dozen on the Net these days but you might enjoy Wanderlust (http://www.salonmagazine.com/wanderlust) for its straightforward and even humorous writing style. If you've ever wondered what it's like to go to Club Med (as I have) check out the article by Po Bronson entitled, "Losing it at Club Med," for the pros and cons of slipping off to that well-advertised domain of hedonism.

Well, it was only a brief moment of fun, a respite from the endless job of configuring computers, downloading patches and plugins and answering e-mail. But it was enjoyable and a harbinger of more to come from the medium that will transform your way of thinking, unite the global village etc., etc.
(For ideas or comments on the weekly Plugged In column contact: russell.blinch(at)reuters.com.)
